pairs.why: In A the open loop runs out of the coil through a knot, so it works as a lasso; in B the loop sits beside the coil, joined only by a stray white ferrule.
A's clamp grips a full truss and the yoke holds the can at a side pivot, while B's short truss stub floats in midair and its beam is a stiff solid cone.
B's keypad is a real calculator layout with digits and operator keys; A's keys are blank, so it could not be used.
A's tabletop has a believable 8x8 chessboard on a column with a base that sits on the grass, while B's oversized top carries a board with too many squares.
B's back canvas is stretched between two posts and its X-legs carry the seat like a real folding chair, while A's back canvas has no top bar and its leg frame shows extra crossing struts.
